summary: Repaired conditional choice-position, numerical-rank and fixed-answer cues. All nine checks and all three final batches pass; 675 grading responses were rerun against the newly finalized shared engine.

source_analysis.skill: Evaluate exact sine values by decomposing a nonspecial angle into two special angles and applying the sine sum or difference identity.
reasoning_steps: Identify supplied decomposition, or construct one if unhinted.
Simplify radical products and combine into an exact answer.
invariants: Sine sum/difference evaluation only, not cosine/tangent evaluation or symbolic-variable expansion.
Special-angle components with manageable radicals and signed quadrant values.
Solutions show identity, special values, arithmetic and final answer.
No decimal approximation substitutes for an exact answer.
permitted_variations: Degree/radian presentation with the same angular value.
Sum versus difference, component order where valid, different supported special angles.
Positive/negative target and small/large magnitude sine; qualifying answer sign and radical sum/difference are incidental, not fixed.
Choice positions and plausible mistake profiles; hint presence and response demand according to band.
source_refs: tutorial a8b2cde2-4c10-51d6-b6f7-3b2a941a1d98 Introduction: These identities can be used to calculate the sine of an angle which is the sum or difference of two special angles.
